bull_bear.body:
- "Annapurna" SSP is recognised as one of the best quality SSP fertilizers available to farmers in West Bengal
- Well-established distributors network in all districts of West Bengal, with a strong dealer and retailer network supporting market share gains
- SSP is economical, easy to handle and a generic fertilizer well-suited to a wide range of crops and soil types, making it a preferred fertilizer
- High tea quality standards maintained, with organized-sector compliance with Maximum Residues Levels (MRL) requirements underpinning export acceptance
- CARE reaffirmed the credit rating on the Company's long term loan and working capital demand loans, reflecting a long term vision for debt management and sufficient liquidity
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on the vagaries of nature across the tea and chemicals businesses — The cautionary statement states that tea and chemicals industries depend upon the vagaries of nature and any adverse or favourable situation can change the whole situation, so actual results could differ materially from projections.
- Continuing price disparity between urea and phosphatic fertilisers — Flagged as the threat in the MD&A Opportunities and Threats section; the disparity results in imbalanced use of fertiliser, which weighs on demand for the Company's phosphatic SSP product.
- High labour intensity of the tea business — The MD&A states the tea industry is highly labour intensive and the Company considers people its biggest asset; total employment was 18576 people as on 31st March 2026, making cost and workforce management structurally significant.
- Pending litigation under Section 58(A) of the Companies Act, 1956 — The Secretarial Audit report observes that the Company had a pending case with the court relating to acceptance of a small amount during the period of approval of a form by the Board and its filing with ROC, and the matter is subjudice.
- Exposure to external factors beyond management control — The cautionary statement notes that operations are influenced by many external and internal factors beyond the control of the Company, so forward looking statements may not be realised.
- Health, safety, security and environment exposure across factory and estate operations — HSSE is stated as a key priority with commitments to the safety of people and assets and protection of the environment; the fertiliser factory runs a full Environment Management System and Occupational Health & Safety Management System, indicating the operational hazard profile being managed.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company grows and manufactures CTC and orthodox tea from its own estates (including Dooars, Darjeeling, Cachar and Terai) supplemented by bought leaf, selling domestically and exporting to more than 25 countries. Its fertiliser division, The Jay Shree Chemicals & Fertilisers at Khardah, West Bengal, manufactures Single Super Phosphate sold to farmers through a dealer and retailer network across West Bengal under the well-known "Annapurna" brand. The Company also operates a sugar mill in Bihar producing white sugar from crushed sugarcane, with a refinery and a distillery attached.

- "Annapurna" SSP is recognised as one of the best quality SSP fertilizers available to farmers in West Bengal
- Well-established distributors network in all districts of West Bengal, with a strong dealer and retailer network supporting market share gains
- SSP is economical, easy to handle and a generic fertilizer well-suited to a wide range of crops and soil types, making it a preferred fertilizer
- High tea quality standards maintained, with organized-sector compliance with Maximum Residues Levels (MRL) requirements underpinning export acceptance
- CARE reaffirmed the credit rating on the Company's long term loan and working capital demand loans, reflecting a long term vision for debt management and sufficient liquidity
business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Expand fertiliser market presence by maintaining superior product quality and ensuring wider product availability, with the stated aim of increasing market share
- Commission a 400 TPD granulation plant to strengthen SSP production capacity and market reach
- Increase sugar crushing capacity phase-wise to 8000 TCD, with modifications in the refinery for quality improvement and in the distillery plant
- Grow tea exports, having raised exports to Rs 116.63 Crore from Rs 99.52 Crore, shipping to more than 25 countries with Germany, UAE, Russia, USA, UK and Japan as major markets
- Improve tea yield and quality through soil health initiatives, rain water harvesting water bodies and enhanced shade status for better micro-climate conditions across estates
- Undertake full-fledged cane development in the allocated area with autumn and spring plantation, and a demonstration farm with high quality seed to encourage farmers to plant more area under sugarcane
- Optimise labour efficiency and cut energy and other input costs, and continue cost rationalisation at the Khardah SSP plant
- Maintain a long term vision for debt management with sufficient liquidity to meet all obligations in time
- The fertiliser factory follows a full Environment Management System and Occupational Health & Safety Management System
- All tea estates follow a green environment policy, with afforestation carried out on a regular basis
- HSSE is a stated key priority, with industry-accredited best practices in health, safety and environment used to set and exceed higher benchmarks
- An internal policy on prevention of sexual harassment at workplace with a complaint-lodging mechanism is in place under the POSH Act, 2013; no complaints were reported to the Board during the year
- The Company does not fall within the top 1000 listed entities required to file a Business Responsibility Report under SEBI (LODR); a short BR report on environment, human resources and principle-wise performance is instead included in the MD&A
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: In the fertiliser business, a 400 TPD granulation plant is being commissioned at the Company's Single Super Phosphate operation to strengthen production capacity and market reach, and is expected to commence commercial production by August 2026. In the sugar business, the Company took up a project during the year for a phase-wise increase in sugarcane crushing capacity to 8000 TCD, together with modifications in the refinery for further improvement in quality and certain modifications in the distillery plant. The Single Superphosphate Plant at Khardah, West Bengal improved its performance through cost rationalization and better quality. On the tea side, the Company undertook initiatives to enhance soil health, created water bodies through rain water harvesting and enhanced shade status across estates to improve micro-climate conditions, yield and quality, while cane development work was carried out on a full-fledged basis in the allocated area with autumn and spring plantation and a demonstration farm with high quality seed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Government of India has expressed continued support for the indigenous SSP industry under the "Make in India" initiative
- SSP subsidy was increased by Rs.2142/- per tonne w.e.f 1st April 2025 and by a further Rs.741/- per tonne w.e.f 1st April 2026
- Higher All India tea production (1370 mn kg vs 1285 mn kg) exerted downward pressure on CTC prices and average realization, while orthodox prices remained firm on robust demand from Iran and Middle East countries
- Indian tea exports reached a record volume of about 280 million kgs, up 10%, on strong demand from Iran, Iraq, USA, UAE and China; Tea Board action on Maximum Residues Level content helped exports
- Assam Tea Industrial Special Incentive Scheme 2020 provides 3% interest subsidy on working capital and an orthodox subsidy of Rs 10 per kg for 5 years upto 2027-28
- Ethanol Blended Petrol programme is likely to be advanced towards higher blend amid rising crude oil prices and geopolitical conditions, with a possible push beyond 20% blending providing potential upside to ethanol prices, which augurs well for the sugar industry
- Sugarcane pricing is administered — FRP of Rs.355/- per quintal centrally and a Bihar State Advised Price revised to Rs.390/- per quintal with a Rs.10/- subsidy from the Government
- "Annapurna" brand enjoys strong market acceptance in West Bengal, supported by a strong dealer and retailer network
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
